note.question: How are reference-dependent utility affects price competition in a horizontally differentiated market where consumers’ tastes diverse?
note.overview: Products such as Nike running shoes, Gillette razors, and Gatorade sports drink serve as the standard against which consumers evaluate other members of the category. Empirical evidence suggests that consumers care about not only the consumption utility derived from a product, but also the gain–loss utility in comparison to the reference product of the category. This paper examines how reference-dependent utility affects price competition in a horizontally differentiated market where consumers’ tastes are diverse.

source.quote: Products such as Nike running shoes, Gillette razors, and Gatorade sports drink serve as the standard against which consumers evaluate other members of the category.

In this survey, participants are presented with a situation where they need to buy a product in a speciﬁc category, and then asked to indicate their product choice, consideration set, recalled brands, and the product that serves as the benchmark (or standard) for comparing the quality and price of other products in the category.
We also get their ratings when the second-preferred brand alone is changed to the least-preferred ﬂavor, and then when the price alone is increased by 25% above the reference price.
We examine the pure-strategy equilibrium of the game to understand the strategic behavior of competing ﬁrms.
After observing the prices, consumers make their purchase decisions.
